chapter: Owls, Werlein's and the OK record
title: Minstrel shows and playing for Frank Williams
summary: He recalls the minstrel shows with dances afterward, in Laplace and Sorrento, and playing at the home of Marguerite Clark's husband on St. Charles.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, he asked me about it. And I won't do it. But it's just procrastination. That's the thief of time. And believe me, I am the world's worst on letter writing. But one of these days, I'll send him an epistle. It'll be a little lengthier than a letter. But I fully intend to do so. And I hope it won't. It'll be forthcoming right soon. You might tell him if you will be kind enough, you said you'd call him and let him know about that or let Mr. Harry know about it, about the bass. I caught his show, This Is Your Life. And maybe Billy Kleppinger might remember me during the days of playing with the Invincibles. You might bring that up. And it was during the days that we used to put on, way back there, we put on minstrel shows too. I was quite a minstrel man back in the old days with Bonnie Casey and Dennis Casey and Warren Spawn. Spawn, not Spawn, Warren Spawn. Well, I can't remember Warren's last name right off the bat, but Chester Aikens and Richard Nichols and Joe Ferguson, bank directors and all, you know. We didn't borrow anybody if they wanted to be in the minstrel. And we'd put on a minstrel first part and a little oleo. And then first thing you know, we'd all get on our instruments and play a dance after. And of course, anybody who wanted to stay, we'd charge them a little extra to dance. And we'd have a dance after the minstrel show. We used to put on shows in Laplace and Sorrento and all around Louisiana there. Had a lot of fun out of it and it was quite educational. We met a lot of fine people at the same time. And I used to play a lot for Frank Williams, Mr. Marguerite Clark. He married Marguerite Clark, the famous movie actress, remember. And we used to play up there on Sony at St. Charles. That's where it was.
5120 St. Charles. I worked in that building. Is that right? I catalogued the collection that Doc gave to the library up there.
